translations.title: Let's Not Waste Time
translations.text:
If the sea is infinite and has nets,
if its music comes from the wave,
if dawn is red and sunset green,
if the forest is lushness and the moon a caress,
if the rose opens and scents the house,
if the little girl laughs and scents our life,
if love comes and kisses me and leaves me trembling,

what does any of it matter
while in my neighborhood there is a table without legs,
a child without shoes or an accountant coughing,
a banquet of peelings,
a concert of dogs,
an opera of mange?

We must concern ourselves with healing the seeds,
with bandaging hearts and writing the poem
that will spread to us all.
And create the phrase that embraces the whole world;
we poets should pull out the swords,
invent more colors and write prayers.

Leave laughter at the mouth of the tunnel,
and speak not of private things but sing in a circle;
do not sing to the moon, do not sing to the sweetheart,
do not write ten-line stanzas or make sonnets.

We must, since we know, shout at the powerful,
shout what I am saying: that many live
under sheets of tin with only the clothes they wear, howling,
and mothers who do not comb their children's hair each day,
and fathers who rise early and never go to the theater.

Adorn the humble by placing our verse on their shoulders;
sing to those who do not sing and help them: that is healthy.
Besiege the moneylenders and, with unusual patience, persuade them without disgust.
Thresh in the fields, descend into a mine;
be a diver for a week, visit the homes for the aged,
the prisons, the ruins; play with the little ones,
dance in the leper colonies.

Poets, let us not waste time; let us work,
for too little blood reaches the heart.
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: You Breathe Through Words Ten Thousand Times a Day...
translations.text:
You breathe through words ten thousand times a day,
you swear by love and beauty,
and ten thousand times you cleanse your lungs
by biting the breath of the foreign gust;

but it is all in vain: death, the palate,
the verbal bird that flies from your tongue.
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: I Am of Air, of Air, Like Every Mortal...
translations.text:
I am of air, of air, like every mortal,
of the great, terrible flight, and I am here on my way to the stars;

but I say to you again that we human beings are already so close to one another
that it would be a mistake—if the explosion itself is a mistake—
it would be a mistake not to love one another.
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: The Turbine
translations.text:
Unicuique suum tribuere: to the fish,
its terror; to this ill-fated
Sunday of aluminum in flames, the roar
of its ruin; to
these three hundred or more
Muslims in the airy air over Smyrna, their
raised scimitar, their
Allah without a nose.

Who
among these whos, which
among these whiches sang among the clouds?
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: Aleph
translations.text:
What do I see on this table: tigers, Borges, scissors, butterflies
that never flew, bones
that never moved this hand, empty
veins, unfathomable tabletop?

I see blindness, I see a spectacle
of madness, things speaking by themselves
just to speak, to rush
toward the narrowness of this kind
of kiss that draws them near; I see your face.
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: The X-ray Shows a Rhythmic, Long-Lived Animal...
translations.text:
The X-ray shows a rhythmic, long-lived animal,
irremediable. Farewell,
fanfare, and it is not that we are
safe once the danger of the year two thousand has passed:
the argument of the cells is different, the
mirror is the same, but we will see the face,
the nose, the perversion of the face,
the eyes perched up there.

Not even Borges,
for all his madness.
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: Riddle of the Desiring Woman
translations.text:
Imperfect young woman seeks imperfect man
of thirty-two; requires reading
of Ovid; offers: (a) two dove breasts,
(b) all her light skin
for kisses, (c) a green
gaze to defy the misfortune
of storms;

she does not make house calls
and has no telephone; accepts
attraction by thought. She is not Venus;
she has Venus's voracity.
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: I Look at the Air in the Air, There Will Pass...
translations.text:
I

I look at the air in the air; these years will pass,
how many of dirty wind
beneath the eyelid, how many
of exile,

II

I will eat earth
of the Earth beneath the slabs
of cement; I will become an eye,
I will become surf.

III

Standing
on the rock of identity, I will become this
bone and no other, this
music of mine, horned

IV

because hollow.
A departure
I am, a departure I shall be.
I depart, depart, depart.
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: Lullaby
translations.text:
Great repose had the dead that night:

Have mercy,
Water, on them for their idleness
and their being turned inside out; let them,
Air, neither be poisoned nor grow dizzy
in the vertigo; Fire, accept as flowers
their poor eyelids; nurse them
once more, Earth, with your ancient breasts.

Earth,
Fire, Air, Water, consider the immensity of their hunger.

Great repose had the dead that night.
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: Asthma Is Love
translations.text:
More than the A of amor I stand for the A
of asthma, and I choke
on your absent air; open to me,
my lofty one, my only one anchored there; no good
is the wooden airplane in which you lie, glass
and all, on those plunging boards, inside
which you are no longer, your slenderness
is no longer there, your great
beautiful feet, your spine
of a pharaoh's mare; and this breathing
is so hard. You
understand me: asthma
is love.
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.
